topics.label: Introduction and course overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the cancer biology lecture series, outlines the multidisciplinary student cohort, and sets out the key learning outcomes.

topics.label: Genetic origins and differentiation failure in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define cancer as a breakdown of normal cellular differentiation and tissue architecture driven by accumulated genetic alterations, while evaluating laboratory models used to study tumor cells.

topics.label: Invasion, progression, and classification of benign and malignant tumors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how benign and malignant tumors are distinguished from one another through their capacity for tissue invasion, histological progression, and diagnostic nomenclature.

topics.label: Mechanisms of cancer morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the physical, physiological, and systemic processes through which primary and metastatic tumors cause clinical illness and death.

topics.label: Epidemiological and comparative incidence of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics analyze patterns of cancer incidence and mortality across different human tissue types and examine comparative tumor occurrence across animal species.

topics.label: Clinical presentation and cancer screening strategies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the clinical presentation of tumors and assess the efficacy, histological basis, and diagnostic challenges of population screening methods.

topics.label: Conclusion and practical briefing
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by reiterating the core learning outcomes and directing students toward their upcoming practical sessions and subsequent lectures.
